access_note: The Figshare page and public provider API list 14 station-specific CSV ZIP files and CC BY 4.0. The CSV payloads were not downloaded, so completeness and quality-control flags were not independently tested.
description: The University of Talca research team publishes digitised five-minute rainfall series from 14 mechanical pluviograph stations in central Chile. Figshare lists a separate CSV ZIP for each station and states CC BY 4.0. Coverage spans the Mediterranean-climate region, with station records beginning between 1969 and 1992 and running to 2009. The series can serve as rainfall inputs for runoff models, estimate short-duration storm intensity, or test stormwater and flood-defence design. They are point observations, not a gridded rainfall field, and periods differ across stations. The article reports manual chart digitisation and quality control, but the underlying CSV values and missing-data flags were not inspected. High mountain and solid-precipitation conditions are underrepresented in this network, so direct transfer to snow-fed basins would need other inputs. The catalogued CoCoRaHS precipitation network is related as a separate rainfall source; this deposit is the specific Chilean historical station collection.
